title: Maunakea’s Shadow
caption: The shadow of Maunakea at sunrise, Hawai‘i
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: At sunrise, the blue shadow of Maunakea in Hawai‘i stretches away from the mountain and narrows into an oddly neat triangle. Maunakea is home to the Gemini North telescope, part of the International Gemini Observatory, which NSF NOIRLab operates.

The mountain itself is only roughly triangular and far from a perfect pyramid, so the tidy shape of its shadow needs explaining. The same triangular shadow can be seen from the summits of many mountains and volcanoes at sunrise or sunset.

The explanation is perspective. An observer on the summit is looking down a long corridor of shadow that reaches all the way to the horizon. Its far end is so distant that it seems to taper to a point, whatever the shape of the peak casting it, and a cube or a column would give the same result. Parallel railway lines and long hallways appear to narrow in the distance for the same reason.

understand.summary: A photograph taken at sunrise on Maunakea, credited to the International Gemini Observatory and J. Chu. No camera details or colour mapping are published.
understand.eye: The triangle is an effect of perspective, so an observer on the summit would see the same tapering shape.
